findings.where: docs/plan/active/refresh-wave-2026-09-18/DECISIONS.md:78 ("0225 RECUTS EXACTLY ONE BODY" and D11's "切第六次") and brief-655.md:13 ("0225 RECUTS EXACTLY ONE BODY") and :15 (`_subledger_classify_entry` listed as a NON-REGRESSION pin to be re-asserted byte-identical) vs. packages/db/migrations/0225_trade_invoices.sql:1-68 (MEASUREMENT 2 header) and :1884-2030 (the two extra recuts) and reports/655-final.md's "Scope deviation" section
findings.what: DECISIONS.md and brief-655.md both bind #655 to recut EXACTLY ONE body, `clara._record_journal_entry_core`, with `_subledger_classify_entry` explicitly named as one of the FIVE bodies to be pinned byte-identical (never modified) in the tail. The merged branch instead recuts THREE governed bodies -- `_record_journal_entry_core`, `_subledger_classify_entry` (new LADDER 3T) and `_tf_subledger_item_belt` (a second lawful source for its bill/invoice arms) -- and drops `_subledger_classify_entry` from the non-regression-pin set entirely, substituting a body the brief never named (`_tf_subledger_entry_belt`) in its place. `_subledger_classify_entry` is a shared classifier with a caller set of SIX across other lanes (staff claims, FA, corrections, close), so widening it is exactly the kind of blast-radius change DECISIONS' "one narrow door" ruling exists to prevent from happening without sign-off.
findings.failure_scenario: The branch as merged does not honour a binding DECISIONS ruling. If the orchestrator does not explicitly ratify the widening (updating DECISIONS.md/brief-655.md to say #225 recuts three bodies, not one), a later reviewer or a from-scratch chain auditor relying on DECISIONS.md's literal text will believe the wave's sole `_subledger_classify_entry`/`_tf_subledger_item_belt` behaviour is still whatever 0037 shipped, when in fact a new LADDER 3T and a second lawful item-belt source now sit inside a body six other callers depend on.
findings.evidence: Read DECISIONS.md D11 and its §1 table (0225's row lists only `_record_journal_entry_core` as a recut) and brief-655.md's "0225 RECUTS EXACTLY ONE BODY" line and its five-name non-regression-pin list (`_subledger_classify_entry` among them); read packages/db/migrations/0225_trade_invoices.sql:30-68 ("MEASUREMENT 2 ... WORK-ORDER rule 6: this widens the brief's ONE recut to THREE") and the T.2/T.3 tail census at :2370-2425 which recuts `_record_journal_entry_core`, `_subledger_classify_entry` and `_tf_subledger_item_belt` and re-pins `_tf_subledger_entry_belt` as non-regression instead; ran the branch's own regression suites live on the 655 rig to confirm the widening does not (yet) break other callers -- `x37-wave-c-a-subledger.test.mjs` 39/39 pass and `fixed-asset-acquisition.test.mjs` 21/21 pass (both exit 0, matching reports/655-final.md's counts) -- which shows the deviation is technically sound but does not make it authorised.
findings.fix: This is a governance action, not a code fix: the worker measured and disclosed the necessity correctly (WORK-ORDER rule 6, migration header MEASUREMENT 2, final report's "Assumptions" #1 and "Scope deviation" section all flag it and explicitly ask for orchestrator confirmation). The orchestrator must either (a) ratify the three-body recut by rewriting DECISIONS.md's D11/§1 row and brief-655.md's "EXACTLY ONE BODY" / non-regression-pin list to match what actually shipped, or (b) direct a follow-up that unwinds `_subledger_classify_entry`/`_tf_subledger_item_belt` back to the originally authorised single-recut shape. Do not accept the branch as DECISIONS-compliant until one of those happens.

findings.where: packages/db/migrations/0225_trade_invoices.sql (_assert_trade_invoice_basis: the `invalid_kind` raises at the null-particulars guard, the unrecognised-`kind` guard, the non-MYR currency guard, and the non-object `tax_facts` guard) vs. packages/runtime/lib/trade-invoice-basis.ts:216 and apps/web/messages/en.json:1653
findings.what: The door overloads the single reason token `invalid_kind` across four semantically different failures (malformed/missing particulars object, an unrecognised `kind` value, a non-MYR currency, and a non-object `tax_facts`), but the runtime module and the web message catalogue both map `invalid_kind` to one fixed sentence, "A trade invoice is either a sales invoice or a supplier bill." This contradicts the report's own framing of `invalid_kind` as "a measured fifteenth token" meaning specifically an unrecognised kind, and DECISIONS.md:50's "the door's own raise ladder is the contract" principle, under which each reason should name one thing.
findings.failure_scenario: A caller that reaches `_assert_trade_invoice_basis` with a non-MYR currency or a malformed `tax_facts` object (bypassing the web form's own zod/currency-literal guard -- e.g. a future direct API caller, the not-yet-built chatTurn_v21 tool, or a batch/import path) would be told "A trade invoice is either a sales invoice or a supplier bill," which is false and would misdirect the person trying to fix the submission.
findings.evidence: grep of `invalid_kind` in packages/db/migrations/0225_trade_invoices.sql shows it raised for: the null/non-object particulars guard, the unrecognised-kind guard, the currency<>'MYR' guard, and the tax_facts-not-an-object guard; packages/runtime/lib/trade-invoice-basis.ts:216 and apps/web/messages/en.json:1653 both key the single string above off the bare `reason==='invalid_kind'`, with no branching on `detail.field`. Not exercised by any p655.polarity.matrix cell (only the unrecognised-kind arm is tested, per trade-invoice.test.mjs:466-474) and not currently reachable through the built web form, since its zod schema already pins `currency` to the literal `"MYR"` and shapes `tax_facts` before the request leaves the browser -- so today's practical severity is low.
findings.fix: Either split the currency and tax_facts-shape guards onto their own reason tokens (documented as a 16th/17th token, consistent with the brief's "if your measured door ends up raising a fifteenth typed reason, the map grows with it" rule), or have the runtime/web message layer branch on `detail.field`/`detail.constraint` to render a currency- or tax-facts-specific sentence when `reason==='invalid_kind'` but the field isn't `kind`.
